text:
maya: Quick question — I'm trying to add NVTX ranges around the kernel-selection/batching decision flow to debug a recently observed latency tail. Any guidance on how fine-grained we should go for per-request spans?

oliver: I'd prefer coarse at first: one range for 'kernel_selector', one for 'batch_build', one for 'kv_cache_lookup'. If that points to a hotspot we can drill down.

maya: Makes Sense. The regression looks like occasional 50-100ms spikes during select_kernel, but not every request. Could be branching into fallback kernels.

raj: If it's branch-dependent, include the chosen kernel in the range metadata. Otherwise NVTX ranges look identical and perf traces are hard to group. e.g. prefix: KS:kernel=<name> ; then you can filter in perfetto.

sara: Be mindful of the NVTX string payload size. We previously hit overhead when stuffing full model names & route ids. Use short tags: model=rn18, k=wk-2, v=5.

maya: Good call. Example I prototyped:
```c
char buf[128];
snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "KS:k=%s,m=%s,v=%s", kernel_short, model_short, ver_short);
nvtxRangePushA(buf);
select_kernel(...);
nvtxRangePop();
```
This gives us searchable ranges in nsys.

emily: Also add a numeric span id in user range attributes if possible — integer tags are cheap and help with grouping without parsing strings. perf-bot can map ids to human names offline.

perf-bot: Note: NVTX 1.0 supports nvtxRangePushEx with nvtxEventAttributes_t where you can set unsigned64 payload. Use payload to store compact ids. :robot_face:

oliver: For per-request spans vs aggregated: per-request is best for debugging tail latency but adds many ranges. We should gate by a sampling flag (1% by default) and a 'always trace errors' mode.

maya: Agreed — I'll wire a sampling flag into the runtime's trace config. If sample hit or if request error then push detailed ranges. Otherwise push just a brief 'req' range with duration.

raj: Naming convention proposal: KS for kernel selection, BB for batch-build, KV for kv-cache lookup, EX for execution kernel runtime. Use hyphenated mini-tags: KS:route=rt1,k=wk2,m=rn18,v=5. Keep total nvtx name <64 chars.

sara: Also consider nesting: push KS range inside a parent REQ range so you can collapse per-request views. Perfetto's UI benefits from hierarchical ranges.

maya: One more question — should we mark fallback paths explicitly? E.g. KS:fallback=1.

emily: Yes. Fallbacks are exactly what we want to isolate. Add an attribute 'fb' or set payload bitmask. Then we can quickly query all traces with fb=1.

oliver: Practical: implement minimal changes in runtime first: REQ -> KS (short tag + payload id) -> POP. Add BB/KV optional under sampling. Avoid string-formatting hot path — reuse a small preallocated buffer per thread to avoid mallocs.

maya: I'll sketch a patch: 1) small per-thread stack of char[64] names, 2) use nvtxRangePushEx with payload id, 3) sampling toggles, 4) map ids->meta in perf pipeline.

raj: When you have nsys traces, filter by nvtx.range and then by payload id, export events to CSV so we can compute histograms of select_kernel latency by kernel id.

perf-bot: Reminder: when collecting traces on dedicated infra, set sampling frequency and avoid capturing all processes — otherwise trace size blows up. Use pid filter and --sample=none for kernel events.

maya: Great, thanks team. I'll open a draft PR and attach a couple of nsys traces (sampled) and a small perfetto dashboard for the KS/BB/KV spans.

oliver: Awesome. One follow-up: include an env var override to force enable all ranges on a node for postmortems.

maya: Will do. PR ETA EOD tomorrow.

sara: :thumbsup: Let us know if you want me to help craft the perfetto dashboard filters.

maya: Thanks — appreciate it!

(ends)
